abstract.text: In this paper, we will apply the tools from number theory and modular forms to the study of the Seiberg-Witten theory. We will express the holomorphic functions a, a D, which generate the lattice Z = n e a + n m a D, (n e, n m) ∈ Z 2 of central charges, in terms of the periods of the Legendre family of elliptic curves. Thus we will be able to compute the transformations of the quotient a D /a under the action of the modular group PSL(2, Z). We will show the Schwarzian derivative of the quotient a D /a with respect to the complexified coupling constant is given by the theta functions. We will also compute the scalar curvature of the moduli space of the N = 2 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory, which is shown to be asymptotically flat near the perturbative limit.

sections.summary: This unit transforms the Seiberg-Witten oneform to the Legendre family, expresses it via a total differential, defines BPS periods π_i, relates them to a,a_D, and introduces the Seiberg-Witten period ϕ and its Q-form ODE.

sections.summary: This unit computes the modular transformations of BPS periods, studies the fixed point λ=1/2, derives {ϕ,τ}=π²/2 θ3⁸ and {a_D/a,τ_sw}=π²/2 θ4⁸, and relates θ4⁸ to the modular form E_{0,4}.
sections.title: Schwarzian derivative of the Seiberg-Witten period

source_span.start_text: 6. Great Picard’s Theorem and the non-perturbative limit

sections.summary: This unit uses Great Picard's Theorem to show that the Seiberg-Witten period ϕ, and hence a_D/a near u=±1, takes real values infinitely many times in small neighborhoods of the non-perturbative limits.
sections.title: Great Picard theorem and non-perturbative limits

source_span.end_text: So the moduli space M is asymptotically flat near λ = ∞, which reflects the property that λ = ∞ (u = ∞) is a perturbative limit of the N = 2 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory.
source_span.start_text: 7. The scalar curvature of the moduli space

sections.summary: This unit computes the moduli-space metric and scalar curvature R, analyzes its singularities at λ=0,1,∞, and shows R diverges exponentially near non-perturbative limits while approaching zero exponentially near the perturbative limit.
sections.title: Scalar curvature of the moduli space

source_span.end_text: It is very interesting to see whether this property has any physical significance in the N = 2 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory.
